questions: Do you have blurred or reduced vision in either eye?
Do you have eye pain or pain with eye movement?
Did these eye-movement symptoms begin after recent nasal or facial surgery?
Have you had recent head or facial trauma?
orders: Bedside ocular motility examination in the nine diagnostic positions of gaze, documenting ductions and versions.
Alternate cover test in primary gaze and in all nine positions to measure ocular misalignment.
Bedside pupillary examination, including direct and consensual light responses and an afferent pupillary defect test.
Noncontrast CT of the orbits and head to assess for orbital fracture, extraocular muscle entrapment, and intracranial traumatic injury.
Forced-duction test of the right eye to assess mechanical restriction of adduction.
Saccadic velocity comparison of right-eye adduction with vestibulo-ocular (oculocephalic) testing to distinguish medial rectus dysfunction from a medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion.
Thin-slice CT of the orbits with multiplanar reconstruction, specifically assessing the right medial rectus muscle, orbital apex, and extraocular muscle entrapment.
Thin-slice CT of the orbits with coronal and sagittal reconstructions to identify a medial orbital-wall fracture and right medial rectus entrapment or contusion.
